question: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother for a rash. The patient had a sore throat a few days ago with symptoms initially well-controlled with lozenges. However, today he had a rash covering his body, which prompted his presentation. The mother states that she did smear an herbal remedy on the rash with no alleviation in symptoms and also gave him a single dose of amoxicillin left over from a previous infection. The patient is up to date on his vaccinations and has no past medical conditions. His temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 102/68 mmHg, pulse is 97/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings in Figures A and B. The rash seen in Figure B is very coarse. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The most likely diagnosis in this case is Scarlet fever, which is caused by group A Streptococcus infection. The patient's history of sore throat, rash, and the appearance of the rash (described as coarse) are consistent with Scarlet fever. The use of amoxicillin can lead to the characteristic rash seen in Scarlet fever due to a hypersensitivity reaction.
